cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't sign the club accounts from a number you read out. Give me the receipt-drawer key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've added it twice. Both totals match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Adding the same omissions twice produces very tidy agreement. We'll check receipt by receipt. The key, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If there's a mistake, the committee will put it on me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we correct it here, together. Start by unlocking the drawer; you can explain each receipt while I check.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 seeks the source-drawer key before signing. A3 corrects B2's double-addition assurance as insufficient coverage, and A5 retains supervisory checking while offering shared correction to overcome B4 fear.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 matching sums invite A3's omitted-item distinction. B4 fear of public blame causes A5 to make unlocking the start of joint private work.

relationship.evidence: B2 believes repeated arithmetic gives assurance; B4 reveals vulnerability. A answers that concern with participation rather than treating B as incompetent in every respect.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's fear to shift the handover into a joint receipt explanation, preserving A's access and professional control.

specificity.evidence: A1 club accounts, signature and receipt drawer establish the needed access; B2 two totals are a clear but incomplete check.
